profile.name: Long Xu
profile.school: School of Electronics and Communication Engineering
bio: I am a Ph.D. candidate at the School of Electronics and Communication Engineering, Sun Yat-sen University. My research explores intelligent computation offloading and resource allocation for edge and vehicular networks.
I am particularly interested in multi-agent reinforcement learning methods that help distributed wireless systems make adaptive decisions under dynamic communication and computing conditions.

research.title: Intelligent Edge Computing
research.description: Adaptive computation offloading for latency- and energy-sensitive services across distributed edge resources.

research.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
research.description: Cooperative decision-making for joint offloading, spectrum, power, and computing-resource allocation.

research.title: Vehicular & Wireless Networks
research.description: Resource optimization for dynamic V2X and wireless sensing environments.

news.text: Our paper on MH-GAT-MAPPO-based adaptive offloading for satellite-terrestrial integrated systems was accepted at FCN 2026.
Our work on enhanced multi-agent deep reinforcement learning for vehicular task offloading appeared in Digital Communications and Networks.
Our adaptive computation offloading work was presented at IEEE WCNC 2025.
Our work on hierarchical target detection and tracking in underwater wireless sensor networks appeared in Digital Communications and Networks.
